facts.text: The Sutherlin Mansion, an Italian Villa-style house built 1857‑1859, now houses the Danville Museum of Fine Arts and History.
During the 1918‑1919 Spanish Influenza outbreak, the Sutherlin Mansion served as a temporary hospital for victims.
The museum’s permanent exhibits include the Camilla Williams Exhibit, celebrating Danville’s internationally acclaimed opera singer.
Danville’s Civil Rights history is highlighted in the museum’s “Movement” exhibit, honoring local leaders and sit‑in protests that prefigured national marches.
The Sutherlin property originally spanned 4 acres and included separate kitchen, laundry, and stables, reflecting its role as an urban plantation.
Visit SoSi, the new regional tourism brand, was unveiled in 2023 to showcase Danville’s unique personality and growing cultural offerings.
